title: Rotate Valve
summary: A valve is mounted on the front face of a wall in front of the hovering aerial manipulator: a large red wheel disc on a short shaft, with a handle bar sticking out of the disc's face toward the robot. Turn the valve: rotate the wheel clockwise, as seen from the robot's side of the wall, by at least 170 degrees from its starting angle.
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane. In front of the robot stands an immovable (kinematic) wall: a slab 0.1 m thick, 2.0 m wide and 2.0 m tall with a concrete-block surface, its front face turned toward the robot. The wall is upright (no tilt in this task); its distance and sideways offset vary between instances. A valve is mounted on the wall's front face with its axis perpendicular to the wall: a dark-blue circular base plate (about 47 cm across) fixed just in front of the wall, a short shaft, and a red disc of the same size that turns with the shaft. On the disc's robot-facing side, off the axis, is a handle bar (square cross-section about 6 cm, 16 cm long, parallel to the axis); at reset it sits directly below the hub (the 6 o'clock position), and it can also spin freely about its own long axis. The valve's height and sideways position on the wall vary between instances. The shaft has no spring and no end stops: it stays at whatever angle it is left, its motion resisted by damping and friction. Nothing moves by itself. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the wall, with its arm at its zero joint configuration (end effector a little ahead of and above the airframe) and the gripper closed.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = arm_link4_roll_joint = 0 rad; arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m with identity orientation and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Wall: kinematic cuboid 0.1 (x) x 2.0 (y) x 2.0 (z) m, nominal centre (2.0, 0.0, 1.0) m and orientation identity (front face the plane x = centre_x - 0.05, normal -x, toward the robot); friction 1.0 static / 1.0 dynamic, restitution 0; visual material NVIDIA Concrete_Block.mdl. At each reset (Isaac Lab mdp.reset_root_state_uniform) the centre becomes (2.0 + dx, 0.0 + dy, 1.0) with dx, dy ~ U(-0.2, 0.2) m independently; the configured pitch range is (0, 0), so the wall keeps the identity orientation (upright, front normal -x). Valve: articulation valve.usd with a fixed root body base_link, self-collisions disabled, solver iterations 16 position / 4 velocity, spawned with scale (1.8, 1.0, 1.8) in the asset's own frame (radial dimensions x1.8, axial dimensions unchanged), mass_props mass = 0.05 kg set on each of the valve's rigid links (the USD authors 0.01 kg per link, 0.005 kg for the handle), contact offset 0.005 m, rest offset 0. At each reset, after the wall, base_link is placed at wall_centre + R_wall (-0.06, vy, vz) with vy, vz ~ U(-0.2, 0.2) m independently (the base-plate centre 0.01 m in front of the wall surface) with orientation R_wall composed with (0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5) wxyz, so the shaft axis (base_link local +z) is world +x, pointing into the wall. Along the axis toward the robot, from the base-plate centre: blue base plate radius 0.234 m, thickness 0.015 m, colour (0.018, 0.115, 0.232); shaft radius 0.108 m from 0.0075 to 0.0475 m; red disc radius 0.234 m from 0.048 to 0.058 m (OmniPBR diffuse tint (0.99, 0.01, 0.01)); handle bar (body handle_link, 0.063 x 0.063 m cross-section, 0.16 m long along the axis) on the robot-facing side of the disc, below the hub at reset (the USD authors its centre 0.135 m out along the axis and 0.144 m below it after scaling, but its joint anchor on the disc is authored elsewhere, so the simulated pose follows the joint: read handle_link's position, which is AM-Bench's goal_pos observation). Joints: base_to_shaft, revolute about base_link +z (world +x), no position limits, reset to 0 rad with zero velocity every episode, Isaac Lab implicit actuator stiffness 0, damping 15.0, friction 0.2 (static and dynamic), effort limit 20, velocity limit 5.0 rad/s; shaft_to_disk fixed; disk_to_handle, revolute about the handle's long axis, unlimited, reset to 0, stiffness 0, damping 10.0, friction 0.1, effort limit 20, velocity limit 5.0 rad/s. Physics material on base plate, shaft and disc: static and dynamic friction 10000; the handle uses the scene default (friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0).
success: Success when the valve has turned clockwise by at least 17/18 pi = 2.96706 rad (170 degrees; valve_target_angle): the unwrapped angle of the revolute joint base_to_shaft, counted from its 0 rad at the reset, is >= 2.96706 rad. Positive is the right-hand rotation about the shaft axis base_link +z, which points into the wall (world +x): clockwise when viewed from the robot's side, so a handle starting straight below the hub first moves toward world +y (the robot's left) and at 170 degrees is 10 degrees short of straight up. The joint has no limits, and PhysX reports its position wrapped into [-pi, pi] (s.objects() shows that raw value): AM-Bench's check compares that raw value, which a counter-clockwise turn of 190 degrees would also bring to +170 degrees, so the tooling (and the grader, with the same tooling) gives the check the unwrapped angle instead, the sum of the joint's per-step changes since the reset, readable as s.valve_angle() (rad). Only a clockwise turn counts; turning the wheel back counter-clockwise subtracts. AM-Bench also reports a subtask criterion valve_engaged (joint position >= 0.05 x 17/18 pi = 0.1484 rad); it is informational only. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 20 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 2400 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 2399th step.

difficulty_note: The wheel has to be turned through nearly half a revolution in one direction against joint damping and friction, in front of a wall, and the valve's place on the wall changes per instance.
standard_notes: The valve's pose and angle are not given: the red disc, the blue base plate and the handle have to be located with the onboard cameras, and the turned angle can only be judged from the handle's position around the hub. Clockwise refers to the view from the robot's side of the wall.
